To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

SARS Cov 2 elicits a broad and highly functional T cell response in exposed individuals and convalescent patients with a history of mild COVID 19 and that these SARS CoV2 specific T cells display a stem like memory T cell phenotype.
SARS CoV-2 specific memory T cell responses are detectable in individuals with a history asymptomatic or mild COVID-19.

SARS CoV-2 elicits robust and polyfunctional memory T cell responses in individuals with a history mild or asymptomatic COVID-19, suggesting that natural infection may prevent severe recurrent episodes of COVID-19.

The main takeaway from our work is that
SARS Co V 2 elicits a strong and durable T cell memory response in convalescent individuals.
SARS Cov 2 elicits broad and functional T cell memory responses in exposed family members and asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic convalescent individuals.

SARS Co V 2 specific memory CD8 T cells are highly polyfunctional, display an effector memory phenotype and are present in antibody serone negative exposed individuals as well as in individuals with asymptomatic or mild COVID 19, indicating that these individuals will likely be protected from reinfection.
